controls: Project-scoped task/channel lookup remains before route result
Approval-required owner gate and canonical published replay retained
Task dry-run reports direct execution false while adapter readiness remains NOT_CHECKED/null
Facade and VkPublisher task methods reject before credentials, refresh or provider
MCP raw-direct VK channel returns BLOCKED after scoped channel resolution, before provider/event writes
Legacy effective channel is resolved read-only before batch/manual/reset writes; VK and unknown held; known non-VK flow retained
No API/alternate-browser fallback, direct queue, lease reset or synthetic fact is created
Explicit legacy channel assignment never falls back when scoped lookup fails; default resolution is only for channel_id=null
Legacy inner provider lookup uses the same scoped explicit-or-truly-unassigned resolver; a null/VK result is held without catch-driven rollback/reset
decomposition: Existing oversized task and legacy modules receive only guard calls/selection integration. Effective legacy-channel classification is extracted to a small typed module; no broad module refactor.
limitations: Guard coverage is application-owned publication entrypoints, not global enforcement of external AI/computer-use tools
Raw vk.service transport remains callable for its library tests; guarded task/facade/MCP/legacy routes cannot invoke it for VK owned publication
Legacy unsupported VK rows remain held without DB state rewrites; scheduler returns zero with blocked-route diagnostic
Readiness/session/provider status was not checked, and registered adapter functionality for other tasks is not implied

Legacy channel classification is not race-atomic canonical017 fencing: a batch publishing claim can precede later binding disappearance. Regression observes one claim followed by zero fallback/provider/reset writes; the held row needs repair rather than blind retry.
verification_error_resolved: One targeted run failed Telegram1099 import due missing TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN; rerun used explicit dummy offline token and passed49.
